item.title: Squeak 2.26.2
item.description:
• Multiplayer: members can message and answer shared threads and run their own agents, shown as "Powered by ... · Flotilla".
  • The owner controls what each member may do, and what each thread allows, from the People menu and the thread's lock menu.
  • Changes apply live, without restarting a thread.
  • Replies to Claude/Codex running in Terminal now come with the external add-ons.

Also in 2.26.1

  • The chat is rebuilt: a new message never shows old work, steps only grow in place, the view stays where you left it, and shared threads show everyone's messages in one order.
  • A stream keeps its tabs: going Home and back no longer drops thread tabs, and opening an older thread from the Dashboard, a search or a notification adds a tab beside the others instead of replacing them. Each stream's tabs also survive a relaunch.
  • A Markdown file (.md, .markdown, .mdx) opens as a rendered preview with a Preview | Source switch in its header: headings, lists, task lists, tables, code with Copy, quotes and images next to the file. Edit switches to the source and Done returns to your last pick.

Also in 2.26.0

  • Settings has a Devices page, not a pairing page: the iPhones and browsers signed in to your account, how each got here, and Remove. "Pair an iPhone..." and the QR sheet are gone, and so is the note that pairing always waits for you.
  • Your own iPhone or browser joins by signing in with the same account. "Ask before adding my own devices" now means one click: a notification with Approve, or Settings > Devices. There is no code to compare.
  • Setting up Squeak no longer shows a QR code for the phone step on Squeak's cloud; it says to sign in on your iPhone. The QR step stays only for an install still on its own server.
  • A Mac can't be flooded with new device keys: it adds at most five of your own devices a minute.
  • A chat that fails to start now leaves its reason in Squeak's log, and stopping a chat ends its agent process instead of leaving it behind.
  • Quitting Squeak puts the Mac's sleep, fans and frozen apps back even if one step is slow, and logs which step was.
  • The New chat project list opens faster, no longer waiting on git.
  • Squeak writes less to the cloud while you watch a working chat, and re-checks less often while its live connection is healthy.
  • The old shared server and the Conductor relay test add-on are gone; no setting changes.
  • A chat waiting on Claude says "Waiting for Claude" instead of a stuck "Thinking...".
  • Very large chats offer Compact or Continue in a new thread, and compact automatically at 200k tokens.
  • A dropped connection shows a clear failure with Try again.
